title: The Day a Lake Disappeared Into the Earth

scenes.narration: In 1980, an entire lake in Louisiana suddenly began disappearing down a hole.
And somehow, everyone survived.
Lake Peigneur was a shallow freshwater lake.
But underneath it was something most people couldn't see:
a massive underground salt mine.
On November 20th, an oil crew was drilling from a platform on the lake.
Then their drill apparently punched into the mine below.
Water started pouring underground.
At first, the opening was small.
But fresh water began dissolving the salt.
The hole grew.
And Lake Peigneur turned into an enormous whirlpool.
The drilling platform disappeared.
Barges were dragged toward the vortex.
Trees and chunks of shoreline vanished into it.
Meanwhile, more than 50 workers were underground in the salt mine.
They evacuated as water rushed into the tunnels.
Amazingly, no human lives were lost.
But then things got even stranger.
The lake was connected to the Gulf of Mexico by the Delcambre Canal.
As the lake drained, the canal's flow reversed.
Water began rushing backward toward the empty lake, creating a temporary waterfall as it poured into the newly formed depression.
Eventually, the flooded mine filled and the lake returned.
But it wasn't the same lake anymore. What had been a shallow freshwater lake became dramatically deeper and increasingly salty.
One drilling accident hadn't just swallowed a lake. It had permanently rewritten the landscape.
